scenes.title: A Truth Universally Acknowledged
scenes.summary: Ironic narrator states the marriage-market truth, then opens in the Bennet household as Mrs. Bennet announces Netherfield Park is let at last while Mr. Bennet answers with dry taciturnity.

scenes.title: Who Has Taken Netherfield
scenes.summary: Prompted to reveal more, Mrs. Bennet details the newcomer: a young, single man of large fortune from the north named Bingley, to take possession before Michaelmas, a fine thing for their girls.

scenes.title: You Must Visit Him
scenes.summary: Mrs. Bennet presses her design that Bingley marry one of their daughters and insists Mr. Bennet must visit him at once; he deflects with teasing compliments and refusal to engage.

scenes.title: Sparring and Character Verdict
scenes.summary: Banter sharpens over which daughter Bingley might choose, Lizzy's quickness, and Mrs. Bennet's poor nerves, closing with the narrator's verdict on Mr. Bennet's sarcastic reserve and Mrs. Bennet's marriage obsession.

scenes.title: Mr. Bennet's Teasing
scenes.summary: Mr. Bennet conceals that he has already called on Mr. Bingley and dryly teases his family. Mrs. Bennet complains about Mrs. Long and introductions while Elizabeth, Kitty, and Mary are drawn into the ironic banter, building fretful domestic tension.

scenes.title: The Reveal and Rejoicing
scenes.summary: Mr. Bennet reveals he has already visited Mr. Bingley, turning resentment into astonished joy. Mrs. Bennet erupts in rapture and self-congratulation as Mr. Bennet withdraws, and the evening dissolves into eager scheming about Bingley's return visit, dinner, and dancing at the ball.

scenes.title: Waiting for Mr. Bingley
scenes.summary: At Longbourn the Bennets pump Mr. Bennet in vain for details of Mr. Bingley and live on Lady Lucas's glowing secondhand report. Hopes of dancing leading to love run high, a brief visit and a deferred dinner invitation cause alarm, then relief as news of the Netherfield party for the assembly ball arrives.

scenes.title: The Assembly Ball and the Slight
scenes.summary: At the assembly Bingley charms everyone with his handsome, lively openness while Darcy is first admired for wealth and looks, then despised as proud and disagreeable. Seated for lack of partners, Elizabeth overhears Bingley urge Darcy to dance and Darcy's cold dismissal of her as merely tolerable, which she retells with spirited amusement.

scenes.title: Good Spirits Return to Longbourn
scenes.summary: The Bennets return to Longbourn in good spirits, Jane much admired and distinguished by Bingley and his sisters, the younger girls never without partners. Mrs. Bennet breathlessly begins her report to Mr. Bennet, dwelling on Bingley dancing with Jane twice.

scenes.title: Mr. Bennet Stops the Finery
scenes.summary: Mr. Bennet impatiently begs his wife to say no more of Bingley's partners and protests against any description of finery. Mrs. Bennet turns with bitterness to relate Mr. Darcy's shocking rudeness to Lizzy, denouncing him as disagreeable and conceited.

scenes.title: Sisters Alone: Praise for Bingley
scenes.summary: Alone after the ball, Jane warmly praises Bingley while Elizabeth teases her affectionately about her habit of liking everyone and defends her own more critical judgment, including doubts about Bingley's sisters.

scenes.title: The Truth About the Bingleys
scenes.summary: The narration coolly reveals the Bingley sisters as proud, conceited women of trade fortune, and explains Bingley's inherited wealth, easy temper, and impulsive tenancy of Netherfield.

scenes.title: Bingley and Darcy: Opposites
scenes.summary: Bingley's open, likable nature is contrasted with Darcy's haughty reserve through their opposite impressions of the Meryton assembly, ending with the sisters approving Jane as a sweet girl.

scenes.title: The Lucases of Lucas Lodge
scenes.summary: The narrator introduces the Lucas family of Lucas Lodge, Sir William's knighthood and good-natured civility, Lady Lucas, and Charlotte as Elizabeth's intimate friend, leading into the Lucases' morning-after visit to Longbourn to discuss the ball.

scenes.title: Talking Over the Ball
scenes.summary: Over lively post-ball gossip at Longbourn, the party dissects Bingley's marked admiration for Jane, Darcy's slight of Elizabeth as merely tolerable and his silence toward Mrs. Long, debating whether his pride is excusable, until the visit dissolves in Mrs. Bennet's scolding of young Lucas about wine.

scenes.title: Jane's Quiet Attachment Observed
scenes.summary: After the visits between Longbourn and Netherfield, Elizabeth notes Bingley's clear admiration and Jane's growing love for him, guarded by her composure and cheerfulness from public notice, and mentions it to Charlotte Lucas.

scenes.title: Encouragement Versus Sincerity in Love
scenes.summary: Charlotte argues Jane must openly show affection to fix Bingley, while Elizabeth defends Jane's sincere restraint and lack of design, leading Charlotte to claim happiness in marriage is entirely chance.

scenes.title: Darcy Watches Elizabeth
scenes.summary: Narration reveals Darcy is unwillingly fascinated by Elizabeth, watching her at Sir William Lucas's party. Elizabeth notices his stare and, egged on by Charlotte, boldly teases him about listening to her conversation.

scenes.title: Music and Dancing at Lucases'
scenes.summary: Pressed by Charlotte, Elizabeth gives a pleasing but modest song, then yields the instrument to Mary, whose vain, pedantic concerto gives way to lively Scotch and Irish airs and impromptu dancing.

scenes.title: Sir William's Awkward Matchmaking
scenes.summary: Darcy stands in silent disapproval of the dancing until Sir William Lucas corners him in stilted small talk and tries to force him and Elizabeth to dance together. Elizabeth firmly refuses, leaving Darcy politely rebuffed yet more impressed.

scenes.title: Fine Eyes and Jealous Teasing
scenes.summary: Miss Bingley presumes Darcy is disgusted by the company and mocks them, but Darcy confesses he was meditating on the pleasure of Elizabeth Bennet's fine eyes. She jealously jokes about his marriage while he remains indifferently amused.

scenes.title: Entailment and Militia Excitement
scenes.summary: Exposition of the Bennet entailment and family connections, shifting to the lively gossip of Meryton where Lydia and Catherine are enthralled by the newly arrived militia regiment and its officers.

scenes.title: The Silliest Girls in the Country
scenes.summary: Witty domestic sparring as Mr. Bennet coolly calls his two youngest daughters silly, Mrs. Bennet defends them, and Lydia chatters on about Colonel Forster and Captain Carter.

scenes.title: The Netherfield Invitation and Rain Scheme
scenes.summary: A note from Caroline Bingley invites Jane to dine at Netherfield; Mrs. Bennet schemes to deny the carriage and force Jane to ride in threatening rain so she must stay the night, and the rain duly traps her there.

scenes.title: Jane Taken Ill
scenes.summary: Morning brings Jane's note that she is ill with cold after getting wet; Mr. Bennet ironically reproaches his wife while Mrs. Bennet remains delighted Jane is detained and refuses alarm.

scenes.title: Elizabeth Walks to Netherfield
scenes.summary: Anxious Elizabeth resolves to walk the three muddy miles to Netherfield despite her mother's objections, accompanied as far as Meryton by Catherine and Lydia hoping to glimpse Captain Carter, then pressing on alone over fields and stiles.

scenes.title: Surprise in the Breakfast Parlour
scenes.summary: Elizabeth enters the Netherfield breakfast-parlour muddy from her walk, astonishing Mrs. Hurst and Miss Bingley, whose politeness masks contempt; Bingley greets her with kindness, Darcy watches with mingled admiration and disapproval, and Hurst cares only for breakfast.

scenes.title: Vigil and Invitation to Remain
scenes.summary: Elizabeth finds Jane feverish and confined to her room; after the apothecary orders bed rest and draughts, Elizabeth nurses her through the day and, at Jane's distress at parting, accepts Miss Bingley's invitation to remain at Netherfield.

scenes.title: An Uncomfortable Dinner
scenes.summary: At dinner Elizabeth gives a poor report of Jane's cold to polite but indifferent company. Only Bingley's genuine anxiety and attention comfort her, while the others ignore or dismiss her.

scenes.title: Scorn for Her Wild Looks
scenes.summary: After Elizabeth leaves to attend Jane, Miss Bingley and Mrs. Hurst attack her manners, wild looks, and muddied petticoat. Bingley defends her affectionate sisterliness, while Darcy coolly praises her fine eyes brightened by exercise.

scenes.title: Contempt for Low Connections
scenes.summary: Mrs. Hurst and Miss Bingley turn to mocking the Bennets' low connections, laughing over an attorney uncle in Meryton and another near Cheapside. Bingley insists it does not lessen them, but Darcy agrees it ruins their chance of respectable marriages.

scenes.title: Sickroom Vigil and the Card Table
scenes.summary: Elizabeth nurses the still-ill Jane until she sleeps, then joins the loo party below. She declines high play to read, prompting surprise from Hurst and scorn from Miss Bingley, softened by Bingley's kind offer of his library.

scenes.title: Praise of Pemberley
scenes.summary: Miss Bingley pivots to flatter Darcy over his small book collection versus the noble library at Pemberley. Darcy responds with pride, Caroline urges Charles to model his future estate on Pemberley, and Bingley teases her ambitions.

scenes.title: What Is an Accomplished Woman
scenes.summary: Elizabeth sets aside her book to watch the cards, sparking a lively debate on what makes a young lady truly accomplished. Darcy sets an impossibly high standard of music, languages, and extensive reading, which Elizabeth wittily challenges before Hurst ends the talk.

scenes.title: Jane Grows Worse
scenes.summary: After Elizabeth leaves, Miss Bingley calls her arts for captivation mean, winning Darcy's assent. Elizabeth returns with news Jane is worse; Bingley insists on sending for Mr. Jones while his sisters propose a London physician, then soothe themselves with duets.

scenes.title: Morning News and Mother's Arrival
scenes.summary: Elizabeth spends the night with Jane, who is improving. Mrs. Bennet hurries to Netherfield with Kitty and Lydia, is relieved Jane is not in danger but glad she must stay, and joins the breakfast parlour where Bingley and Miss Bingley assure her Jane will be kept.

scenes.title: Sweet Temper and Hasty Character
scenes.summary: Mrs. Bennet praises Jane's sweet temper and Netherfield's prospect while pressing Bingley to stay, and Elizabeth teases Bingley about doing everything in a hurry and being easily seen through.

scenes.title: Offence in Confined Society
scenes.summary: After Mrs. Bennet reproves Elizabeth, Darcy dismisses country society as confined and unvarying, offending Mrs. Bennet into a sharp retort before he turns silently away, leaving her triumphant.

scenes.title: Country Against London and a Mother's Praise of Jane
scenes.summary: Mrs. Bennet proclaims the country pleasanter than London and accuses Darcy of despising it, forcing a blushing Elizabeth to correct her. While Bingley politely keeps his countenance and Caroline smiles expressively at Darcy, Elizabeth tries to divert her mother by asking after Charlotte Lucas. Mrs. Bennet instead praises Sir William's fashion and breeding, pities the Lucases for want of beauty, and boasts at length of Jane's superior looks and a youthful admirer who wrote verses on her.

scenes.title: Poetry the Food and Starver of Love
scenes.summary: Elizabeth impatiently dismisses the verse-writing admirer and jests that poetry drives love away. Darcy answers that poetry is the food of love, and Elizabeth retorts that it nourishes only strong love while starving a slight inclination, drawing only a smile from Darcy. In the ensuing pause Elizabeth trembles lest her mother expose herself again, as Mrs. Bennet renews thanks to Bingley, orders her carriage, and the youngest daughters prepare to claim his promised Netherfield ball.

scenes.title: Lydia Claims the Ball and Departs
scenes.summary: Bold, high-spirited Lydia abruptly taxes Bingley on his promised Netherfield ball. He gallantly promises it once Jane recovers. Satisfied, Lydia plans an officers' ball in return, then the Bennet party departs, leaving Elizabeth to rejoin Jane while the Netherfield party censures her relations.

scenes.title: The Letter and the Flatterer
scenes.summary: In the Netherfield drawing-room in the evening, Elizabeth watches with amusement as Miss Bingley fawns over Mr. Darcy while he writes to his sister, praising his handwriting, speed, and length while he answers with cool unconcern.

scenes.title: A Debate on Humility and Persuasion
scenes.summary: Bingley's careless writing sparks a witty philosophical spar between Elizabeth and Darcy on humility, indirect boast, precipitance, and yielding to persuasion, with Bingley pleading for an end to argument until Darcy returns to finish his letter.

scenes.title: Music at the Pianoforte
scenes.summary: Miss Bingley plays the pianoforte with Mrs. Hurst singing while Elizabeth turns pages; Elizabeth notices Darcy repeatedly fixing his eyes on her and concludes it must be disapproval, which does not trouble her.

scenes.title: The Reel Invitation
scenes.summary: After Italian songs and a lively Scotch air, Darcy invites Elizabeth to dance a reel; she playfully refuses to give him cause to despise her taste, and he answers with gallantry, finding himself bewitched by her sweetness and archness despite her inferior connections.

scenes.title: Miss Bingley's Mocking Provocation
scenes.summary: Jealous of Elizabeth and anxious to hasten her departure, Miss Bingley walks with Darcy in the shrubbery and tries to provoke him to dislike her by mocking their supposed marriage and criticizing her mother, younger sisters, and impertinence.

scenes.title: Beautiful Eyes and a Gaily Escape
scenes.summary: Darcy calmly turns the teasing aside and admires Elizabeth's beautiful eyes. Joined by Mrs. Hurst and Elizabeth, he remarks on their rudeness in excluding her, but Elizabeth gaily leaves them, rejoicing that Jane is recovering enough to leave her room.

scenes.title: A Pleasant Evening Before the Fire
scenes.summary: After dinner Elizabeth joins Jane in the drawing-room for agreeable conversation, then the gentlemen enter and Bingley devotes himself entirely to Jane while Elizabeth watches with delight. The party settles into quiet inactivity with no cards, Hurst asleep, and Darcy and others reading.

scenes.title: Miss Bingley Watches Darcy Read
scenes.summary: Caroline Bingley watches Mr Darcy's progress through his book as much as her own, repeatedly questioning him and looking at his page without winning him to conversation, until exhausted she yawns over the second volume she chose only to match his and declares the pleasures of reading and a fine library.

scenes.title: Miss Bingley Provokes Talk of a Ball
scenes.summary: Met with silence, Caroline throws aside her book and provokes debate about Charles's proposed Netherfield ball, calling dancing tedious, then parades elegantly about the room to catch the still studious Darcy's eye and at last invites Elizabeth to take a turn with her.

scenes.title: Wit and Pride at the Fireside
scenes.summary: Darcy looks up and declines to join the walk with a teasing remark about secret confidences and fine figures. Elizabeth and Darcy fall into sharp, witty sparring about laughter, pride, vanity, and resentment, with Caroline sidelined as their mutual fascination grows.

scenes.title: A Little Music to Break the Spell
scenes.summary: Tired of being excluded, Caroline calls for music and has the pianoforte opened. Darcy welcomes the interruption, beginning to feel the danger of paying Elizabeth too much attention.

scenes.title: The Refused Carriage and Deferred Departure
scenes.summary: Elizabeth writes for the carriage, but Mrs. Bennet refuses it before Tuesday; fearing intrusion, Elizabeth has Jane ask for Bingley's carriage, and polite pressure delays their departure till the morrow, with Bingley genuinely concerned for Jane's health and Miss Bingley regretting the delay from jealousy of Elizabeth.

scenes.title: Darcy's Resolve and the Sunday Separation
scenes.summary: Darcy, alarmed by his attraction to Elizabeth, resolves to suppress all admiration and pointedly ignores her through Saturday; on Sunday after service the party separates with relief, Miss Bingley suddenly civil to Elizabeth and effusive to Jane, and Elizabeth departs in high spirits.

scenes.title: Home Again to Longbourn
scenes.summary: Jane and Elizabeth return to Longbourn to a cool welcome from their mother and quiet pleasure from their father, finding Mary absorbed in study and Catherine and Lydia full of regiment gossip about dinners, a flogging, and Colonel Forster's rumored marriage.

scenes.title: An Addition to Our Family Party
scenes.summary: At breakfast Mr. Bennet teases his family with news of an expected stranger, letting Mrs. Bennet assume it is Mr. Bingley before revealing it is a cousin they have never met, sparking eager curiosity.

scenes.title: The Odious Entail
scenes.summary: Mr. Bennet names his cousin Mr. Collins, the heir to Longbourn, prompting Mrs. Bennet's bitter railing against the entail while Jane and Elizabeth try in vain to reason with her.

scenes.title: The Olive Branch Letter
scenes.summary: Mr. Bennet reads Collins's long, pompous letter aloud, in which Collins apologizes for his father's quarrel, boasts of his ordination and patroness Lady Catherine de Bourgh, and proposes a week-long peacemaking visit to atone for inheriting Longbourn.

scenes.title: Making Out Mr. Collins
scenes.summary: The Bennets dissect the letter with amused skepticism, noting its servility to Lady Catherine, its pompous style, and its vague promise of amends, while Mrs. Bennet is softened and the younger girls remain indifferent.

scenes.title: The Punctual Guest at Dinner
scenes.summary: Punctual Mr. Collins arrives, tall, grave and excessively formal, showering the daughters with awkward compliments, admiring the house as his future property, and prolonging an embarrassing apology over dinner.

scenes.title: In Praise of Lady Catherine
scenes.summary: After dinner Mr. Bennet prompts his guest to shine on his patroness, and Mr. Collins delivers a solemn, eloquent panegyric on Lady Catherine de Bourgh's affability, dinners at Rosings, advice to marry, and her sickly daughter Miss de Bourgh, under Mrs. Bennet's eager questioning.

scenes.title: Bennet's Private Amusement
scenes.summary: Mr. Bennet archly compliments Collins on his talent for delicate flattery, Collins complacently explains his studied yet unstudied compliments, and Bennet savors his cousin's absurdity with resolute composure and an occasional glance at Elizabeth.

scenes.title: Sermons Abandoned for Backgammon
scenes.summary: In the drawing-room Collins refuses to read novels, chooses Fordyce's Sermons, and reads with monotonous solemnity until Lydia interrupts with Meryton gossip about Richard and Colonel Forster. Offended by young ladies' disregard for instruction, he abandons reading and joins Mr. Bennet at backgammon.

scenes.title: Mr. Collins's Plan of Atonement
scenes.summary: The narrator sketches Mr. Collins's pride, obsequiousness, and patronage under Lady Catherine, and his plan to atone for inheriting Longbourn by marrying one of the daughters, shifting his settled choice from Jane to Elizabeth after Mrs. Bennet hints Jane will soon be engaged.

scenes.title: A Tedious Walk to Meryton
scenes.summary: Mr. Bennet escapes Collins's pompous chatter by sending him to walk with his daughters to Meryton, where the younger sisters ignore Collins entirely in their eager search for officers and shop novelties.

scenes.title: Wickham Appears, Darcy Freezes
scenes.summary: Denny introduces the handsome newcomer Mr. Wickham to the party, then Darcy and Bingley ride up; Elizabeth is astonished to see Darcy and Wickham stare at each other, change colour, and exchange only the coldest recognition before Bingley rides on.

scenes.title: Gossip at Mrs. Philips's
scenes.summary: At Mrs. Philips's house the nieces gossip about Wickham and secure a dinner and lottery-tickets invitation for the next evening; on the walk home Elizabeth puzzles over the Darcy-Wickham meeting with Jane, while Collins returns delighted by Mrs. Philips's flattering civility.

scenes.title: An Evening at Mrs. Philips's
scenes.summary: The Bennet girls and Mr. Collins arrive at Meryton to find Wickham already invited. Collins fawns over the Philips' drawing-room by comparing it to Rosings, while the girls wait impatiently for the officers to join them. When Wickham enters, Elizabeth is struck by his superiority in looks and manners, and he seats himself by her as card tables are placed.

scenes.title: Wickham Begins His Tale
scenes.summary: Seated at the lottery table, Elizabeth hopes to hear of Darcy and is relieved when Wickham raises him himself. Wickham probes Darcy's stay at Netherfield, claims lifelong connection to his family, and hints at great ill usage and painful regrets, centering on the late Mr. Darcy as his truest friend. Elizabeth listens with growing interest.

scenes.title: The Stolen Living
scenes.summary: Wickham unfolds his full grievance: bred for the church and promised the best Pemberley living by old Mr. Darcy, he lost it to another man through young Darcy's pride, jealousy and alleged charge of extravagance. Elizabeth reacts with shock and indignation, deeming Darcy dishonest and inhuman. Wickham extends the portrait to Darcy's pride, generosity, guardianship of his proud sister Miss Darcy, and childhood shared at Pemberley.

scenes.title: Darcy and Bingley Discussed
scenes.summary: Elizabeth wonders how amiable Bingley can be intimate with Darcy, and Wickham explains that Darcy can please when he chooses, showing a different face to his equals in consequence.

scenes.title: Whist Ends and Supper
scenes.summary: The whist party ends and Collins pompously dismisses his losses thanks to Lady Catherine. Wickham learns the connection, reveals Lady Catherine is Darcy's aunt and hints at his destined union with Miss de Bourgh. Supper ends cards, Wickham charms all, and Elizabeth returns home full of him.

scenes.title: Sisters Debate Wickham and Darcy
scenes.summary: Elizabeth confides Wickham's history of Darcy's ill-treatment to Jane in the shrubbery. Jane, unwilling to condemn either man, suggests mutual deception, while Elizabeth insists on Wickham's truthfulness and Darcy's guilt, leaving them divided and Jane anxious for Bingley.

scenes.title: Invitation to the Netherfield Ball
scenes.summary: Bingley and his sisters arrive in person to invite the family to the Netherfield ball and hurriedly depart. The Bennet women glow with anticipation, each picturing dancing, Wickham, and happy hours with friends.

scenes.title: Elizabeth Jest Traps Her Into Collins Dances
scenes.summary: In high spirits, Elizabeth teasingly asks Mr. Collins if he will dance at Netherfield, and is surprised when he declares no scruples and promptly solicits her hand for the first two dances.

scenes.title: Hunsford Design Dawns During Rainy Wait
scenes.summary: Elizabeth regrets losing the dances meant for Wickham to Collins, realizes Collins has singled her out for Hunsford, and endures days of confining rain with the family impatient for Tuesday's ball.

scenes.title: Wickham's Absence
scenes.summary: Elizabeth arrives eager to meet Wickham, only to learn he has gone to town. Hearing he wished to avoid Darcy, her disappointment sharpens into open displeasure against Darcy.

scenes.title: Dances of Mortification
scenes.summary: Elizabeth unburdens herself to Charlotte Lucas, then endures two mortifying dances with the awkward, apologetic Mr. Collins, feeling ecstasy at her release.

scenes.title: A Surprise Partner Accepted
scenes.summary: Revived by dancing and talking of Wickham, Elizabeth is caught off guard into accepting Darcy as a partner, frets over her lapse, and faces their silent, tense set with amusement and dread.

scenes.title: A Tense Dance and Sharp Words
scenes.summary: Standing up together in strained silence, Elizabeth and Darcy trade sharp, witty remarks. Her mention of a new acquaintance turns the sparring serious as Darcy slights Wickham and she defends him.

scenes.title: Interrupted Talk and Cold Parting
scenes.summary: Sir William's pompous interruption breaks their quarrel. When dancing resumes, Elizabeth presses Darcy on forgiveness and prejudice, and they part in mutual dissatisfaction.

scenes.title: Miss Bingley's Warning Against Wickham
scenes.summary: Miss Bingley accosts Elizabeth to discredit Wickham as the steward's son who has treated Darcy infamously, which Elizabeth angrily rejects as malice and ignorance before turning with relief to Jane's evident happiness.

scenes.title: Jane Reports Bingley's Defence of Darcy
scenes.summary: Jane reports that Bingley vouches for Darcy's honour and probity while condemning Wickham as unrespectable and imprudent, but Elizabeth, noting Bingley knows Wickham only through Darcy, refuses to be convinced and keeps her former opinion of both men.

scenes.title: Collins Introduces Himself to Darcy
scenes.summary: Elated to discover Darcy is Lady Catherine's nephew, Mr. Collins ignores Elizabeth's warnings and introduces himself, earning distant civility and contempt which he blissfully misreads as approval.

scenes.title: Supper Embarrassments
scenes.summary: At supper Elizabeth burns with shame as Mrs. Bennet loudly boasts of Jane's coming marriage within Darcy's hearing, Mary obliviously sings badly twice, and Mr. Collins delivers a loud, fawning speech.

scenes.title: Persevering Attentions
scenes.summary: Elizabeth finds no amusement, pinned by Mr. Collins who refuses to leave her side despite her entreaties, relieved only by Charlotte Lucas engaging him, while Darcy pointedly never comes near to speak. The Longbourn party is last to depart, kept waiting for their carriages amid the cold impatience of Mrs. Hurst and Miss Bingley, Mr. Collins's long compliments, and Bingley and Jane talking apart.

scenes.title: A Satisfied Departure
scenes.summary: At leave-taking Mrs. Bennet pressingly invites the Netherfield family to Longbourn and secures Bingley's grateful promise to dine with them after his short trip to London. Perfectly satisfied, she quits the house dreaming of Jane settled at Netherfield within months, and of Elizabeth married to Mr. Collins.

scenes.title: An Audience Demanded
scenes.summary: The morning after the ball, Mr. Collins formally asks Mrs. Bennet for a private audience with Elizabeth. Elizabeth begs to avoid it, but Mrs. Bennet insists she stay and hear him, then leaves with Kitty, trapping Elizabeth.

scenes.title: The Solemn Proposal
scenes.summary: Left alone with Elizabeth, Mr. Collins assures her he has her mother's permission and launches into his pompous reasons for marrying: clerical example, happiness, and Lady Catherine de Bourgh's advice, then his plan to lessen the entail loss by choosing a Bennet daughter while professing indifference to her small fortune.

scenes.title: A Plain Refusal
scenes.summary: Elizabeth interrupts to thank him but firmly decline. Collins dismisses it as conventional female coyness and expects to lead her to the altar. She insists she is perfectly serious and ill-suited to him and Lady Catherine, declares the matter finally settled, and rises to leave.

scenes.title: Wilful Self-Deception
scenes.summary: Collins persists that first refusals are mere encouragement, flatters himself his connections and establishment must be desirable given her small portion, and appeals to her parents' authority. Elizabeth asserts she is a rational creature speaking truth, not tormenting him, then silently withdraws to seek her father's decisive negative.

scenes.title: Felicitations Gone Awry
scenes.summary: Mrs. Bennet bursts in to celebrate the supposed engagement, and Collins recounts Elizabeth's refusal as bashful modesty. When Mrs. Bennet calls Lizzy headstrong, Collins coolly doubts such a wife would suit his happiness, forcing Mrs. Bennet to backtrack.

scenes.title: The Library Verdict
scenes.summary: Mrs. Bennet drags Mr. Bennet to force the marriage, but he summons Elizabeth and settles it with deadpan irony: she will be estranged from her mother if she refuses Collins, and from him if she accepts. Mrs. Bennet is furious, Mr. Bennet reclaims his library.

scenes.title: Coaxing, Refusal, and Wounded Pride
scenes.summary: Mrs. Bennet repeatedly coaxes and threatens Elizabeth to accept Collins, Jane mildly refuses to interfere, Elizabeth remains resolute, and Collins nurses his wounded pride alone without real regret.

scenes.title: Charlotte Finds Fun and Entreaty
scenes.summary: Charlotte Lucas arrives to find Lydia and Kitty gleefully spreading news of the rejected proposal, while Mrs. Bennet begs her to persuade Elizabeth until Jane and Elizabeth's entrance spares her reply.

scenes.title: Nerves and Undutiful Children
scenes.summary: Mrs. Bennet reproaches Elizabeth for refusing marriage, lamenting her nerves, her future maintenance, and declaring she is done speaking to her undutiful child.

scenes.title: Formal Withdrawal
scenes.summary: Mrs. Bennet demands privacy for a talk with Mr. Collins; the other girls withdraw while Collins pompously declares his resignation, withdraws his pretensions to Elizabeth, and apologizes.

scenes.title: Stiff Silence After Refusal
scenes.summary: Stiff, resentful aftermath of Elizabeth's refusal. Mr. Collins punishes her with silence and transfers attentions to Charlotte, while Mrs. Bennet simmers in ill humour, and Elizabeth hopes in vain he will cut his visit short.

scenes.title: A Walk to Meryton with Wickham
scenes.summary: Light, flirtatious social interlude on the walk to Meryton. The sisters commiserate over Wickham's absence from the ball, and Wickham charmingly explains he stayed away to avoid Darcy, walking them home to meet her parents.

scenes.title: The Sudden Removal to London
scenes.summary: A letter from Netherfield arrives for Jane and visibly unsettles her. Upstairs alone with Elizabeth, she reveals it is from Caroline Bingley announcing the whole party has left for London with no intention to return, a sudden removal Elizabeth hears with distrust.

scenes.title: The Painful Prospect of Georgiana Darcy
scenes.summary: Jane reads Caroline's further passages aloud, confirming none will return for winter and confessing the Bingley sisters' hope that Bingley will marry Georgiana Darcy. Jane is hurt and convinced he will not return, while Elizabeth insists it is only Miss Bingley's design.

scenes.title: Sisters Debate Caroline's Meaning
scenes.summary: Anxious, intimate sisterly debate in their room. Jane fears Caroline's letter proves Bingley's indifference and dreads his sisters' disapproval, while Elizabeth insists it is a jealous ploy to separate Bingley from Jane and marry him to Miss Darcy.

scenes.title: Comfort Restored, Mother Lamenting
scenes.summary: From comforting reassurance to comic maternal worry. Elizabeth scorns the idea Bingley will not return and restores Jane's hope, then they tell Mrs. Bennet only of the departure, prompting her lament turning to consolation over future dinners.

scenes.title: A Scheme Secured at Lucas Lodge
scenes.summary: Mr. Collins slips away from Longbourn to propose to Charlotte Lucas, who has deliberately encouraged him to secure him away from Elizabeth. She accepts him for an establishment, and the Lucas family joyfully consents while Charlotte calmly justifies her pragmatic choice.

scenes.title: The Mysterious Farewell
scenes.summary: On his last evening at Longbourn, Collins barely conceals his triumph while hinting at a speedy return, baffling the Bennets. Mr. Bennet teases him about Lady Catherine, Mrs. Bennet speculates he aims at Mary, until the next morning Charlotte arrives to reveal the truth.

scenes.title: An Impossible Engagement Confessed
scenes.summary: In private, Charlotte tells Elizabeth of her engagement to Mr. Collins. Elizabeth bursts out in shock, then forces congratulations, while Charlotte defends her unromantic desire for a comfortable home. Left alone, Elizabeth reflects with humiliation and sorrow on her friend's sacrifice to worldly advantage.

scenes.title: An Unbelievable Announcement
scenes.summary: Sir William Lucas arrives to announce Charlotte's engagement to Mr. Collins. Mrs. Bennet and Lydia react with incredulous rudeness, and Elizabeth steps in to confirm the news and smooth the awkwardness with polite congratulations.

scenes.title: Mrs. Bennet's Resentment
scenes.summary: Mrs. Bennet is overpowered and then vents her feelings, disbelieving the engagement, pitying Mr. Collins, predicting unhappiness, blaming Elizabeth as the cause, and nursing prolonged resentment toward the Lucases.

scenes.title: Amusement and Triumph
scenes.summary: Mr. Bennet savors the irony with tranquil amusement, Jane wishes the couple happiness, Kitty and Lydia are unmoved, and Lady Lucas triumphantly parades her daughter's good fortune at Longbourn.

scenes.title: Silence and Anxious Waiting
scenes.summary: A cool restraint settles between Elizabeth and Charlotte while Elizabeth worries ever more for Jane. With Bingley gone and rumored not to return, Jane waits in concealed anxiety as Mrs. Bennet loudly frets and complains.

scenes.title: The Heir's Return and the Entail Lament
scenes.summary: Mr. Collins returns, absorbed in lovemaking at Lucas Lodge to the family's relief. Mrs. Bennet torments herself with jealous visions of Charlotte supplanting her at Longbourn, culminating in a peevish exchange with Mr. Bennet over the entail.

scenes.title: The Letter Ends Hope
scenes.summary: Caroline Bingley's letter confirms the party settled in London for winter. Hope for Bingley's return is extinguished. Jane finds little comfort except professed affection and news of Bingley with Darcy and Miss Darcy; Elizabeth receives it in silent indignation, blaming Bingley's weak resolution and designing friends while grieving her sister's wounded peace.

scenes.title: Sisters' Sorrow and Defence
scenes.summary: Alone together after Mrs. Bennet's complaints about Netherfield, Jane bravely insists she will forget Bingley and claims only an error of fancy on her side. Elizabeth praises her angelic disinterestedness, then vents dissatisfaction with the world over Charlotte's marriage and Bingley's conduct. Jane gently defends Charlotte, Collins, Bingley and his sisters, urging charitable interpretation; Elizabeth half-yields, and Bingley's name is scarcely mentioned again between them.

scenes.title: Family Raillery and Wickham's Popularity
scenes.summary: Mrs. Bennet continues to repine and hopes Bingley returns in summer, while Mr. Bennet teases Elizabeth about being crossed in love and recommending Wickham. Wickham's open society dispels gloom at Longbourn as his claims against Darcy are publicly canvassed, leaving Darcy condemned as the worst of men by all except the candid Jane.

scenes.title: Parting and Christmas Arrival
scenes.summary: Mr. Collins takes solemn leave of Longbourn to prepare for his bride, and the Gardiners arrive for their usual Christmas visit, introduced as sensible, elegant favourites of the Bennet daughters.

scenes.title: Mrs. Bennet's Grievances
scenes.summary: After presents and fashions, Mrs. Bennet unloads her grievances about lost marriages for Jane and Elizabeth, blaming Elizabeth for refusing Collins, while Mrs. Gardiner deflects out of compassion.

scenes.title: Violent Love Questioned
scenes.summary: Alone, Mrs. Gardiner calls Bingley's departure common inconstancy after brief love, Elizabeth insists friends interfered with a violently decided attachment, and Mrs. Gardiner proposes Jane return with them to London for change of scene.

scenes.title: Custody and Change of Scene
scenes.summary: Elizabeth mocks Darcy for keeping Bingley in custody from Gracechurch Street impurity, predicts Jane will drop Caroline Bingley, yet privately hopes Jane's attractions may reanimate Bingley; Jane accepts the London invitation to see Caroline without danger of seeing him.

scenes.title: A Week of Company and Watchful Concern
scenes.summary: During the Gardiners' week at Longbourn, filled with daily engagements with the Philipses, Lucases, and officers, Wickham is constantly in company. Mrs. Gardiner, made suspicious by Elizabeth's warm praise of him, watches them closely and, seeing their plain preference for each other, grows uneasy and resolves to warn Elizabeth of the imprudence before leaving Hertfordshire.

scenes.title: Derbyshire Remembered and Pemberley Praised
scenes.summary: Wickham pleases Mrs. Gardiner with fresh intelligence of Derbyshire, where she had lived before her marriage. Their shared acquaintance and her memories of Pemberley and esteem for the late Mr. Darcy create an inexhaustible subject, leading her to accept Wickham's account of the present Mr. Darcy and recall him as a very proud, ill-natured boy.

scenes.title: A Warning Against Imprudent Fancy
scenes.summary: Alone together, Mrs. Gardiner seriously cautions Elizabeth not to involve herself or Wickham in an imprudent affection without fortune, appealing to her sense and her father's trust. Elizabeth first answers lightly, then earnestly insists she is not in love with Wickham, sees the imprudence, and promises not to hurry or encourage him.

scenes.title: Advice Received Without Resentment
scenes.summary: Mrs. Gardiner advises Elizabeth to discourage Wickham's frequent visits and not prompt her mother to invite him. Elizabeth owns her fault with a conscious smile, promises upon her honour to do what is wisest, thanks her aunt, and they part without resentment.

scenes.title: Charlotte's Farewell and Wedding
scenes.summary: Collins returns for his imminent wedding while Charlotte pays her farewell visit. Moved and ashamed of her mother's coldness, Elizabeth walks her out and reluctantly promises to visit Hunsford. The wedding occurs, the couple leaves for Kent, and Elizabeth notes their correspondence has lost its former intimacy.

scenes.title: Anxious Waiting for News from Town
scenes.summary: Jane writes from London and Elizabeth waits impatiently for news of the Bingleys. After a week of silence Jane explains a lost letter and reports a brief, unsatisfying call on Caroline, who mentions Bingley is always engaged with Darcy. Elizabeth suspects Bingley is being kept ignorant that Jane is in town.

scenes.title: Jane's Disillusionment
scenes.summary: After four weeks without seeing Bingley and a final short, altered visit from Caroline, Jane can no longer deceive herself. In a pained letter she confesses she was entirely deceived in Miss Bingley's regard, pities yet blames her, suspects duplicity and talk of Miss Darcy and giving up Netherfield, and resolves to end the acquaintance.

scenes.title: Two Disappointments Borne Lightly
scenes.summary: Stung by Jane's letter, Elizabeth abandons all hope in Bingley and his character sinks in her esteem. She then reports with wry composure that Wickham's attentions have transferred to the newly rich Miss King, assuring her aunt her heart was only slightly touched and she feels no hatred, only amused resignation.

scenes.title: Departure for Hunsford by Way of London
scenes.summary: Elizabeth looks forward to the Hunsford visit as a welcome change from home, bids an affectionate farewell to her father and to Wickham, endures a dull chaise journey with Sir William and Maria, and arrives to a joyful reunion with Jane and the Gardiner children in London.

scenes.title: Confidences with Mrs. Gardiner
scenes.summary: Sitting with her aunt at the theatre, Elizabeth learns Jane is still dejected over Bingley and has given up Miss Bingley, then spars good-humouredly in defence of Wickham's pursuit of heiress Miss King, masking her own disappointment with wit.

scenes.title: Invitation to the Lakes
scenes.summary: The evening brightens when Mrs. Gardiner invites Elizabeth to join a summer tour possibly to the Lakes, which Elizabeth accepts with rapturous delight as an antidote to disappointment in men.

scenes.title: The Road to Hunsford
scenes.summary: Elizabeth enjoys the final day's journey with spirits lifted by Jane's good health, and the party eagerly watches for the first sight of the Hunsford Parsonage along Rosings Park.

scenes.title: Reception at the Parsonage
scenes.summary: The travellers arrive at the Parsonage to a warm welcome from Charlotte, while Mr. Collins receives them with unchanged formal civility and leads them into the parlour with ostentatious offers of refreshment.

scenes.title: Display of House and Garden
scenes.summary: Mr. Collins pompously displays the parlour, garden, and prospect of Rosings, which Elizabeth regards with amusement at Charlotte's cheerful endurance, before Charlotte shows her friends the neat and comfortable house without her husband's help.

scenes.title: Dinner Talk of Lady Catherine
scenes.summary: At dinner Mr. Collins boasts of Lady Catherine de Bourgh's condescension and expected invitations to Rosings, and that night alone Elizabeth reflects on Charlotte's contentment, her skill in handling her husband, and the quiet routine ahead.

scenes.title: A Sight at the Garden Gate
scenes.summary: Rushed downstairs by an agitated Maria, Elizabeth discovers the cause of the commotion is two ladies in a low phaeton at the garden gate, whom she first mistakes for Lady Catherine before learning they are Miss de Bourgh and Mrs. Jenkinson.

scenes.title: Bows and an Invitation to Rosings
scenes.summary: Elizabeth mocks Miss de Bourgh's sickly appearance and rudeness while Collins, Charlotte, and a bowing Sir William attend the ladies at the gate, after which Collins announces the whole party is invited to dine at Rosings the next day.

scenes.title: Collins's Triumph
scenes.summary: Mr. Collins exults over the unexpected dinner invitation to Rosings as proof of Lady Catherine's condescension, while Sir William moralizes on great manners and the party spends the day in excited anticipation.

scenes.title: Toilette Fears
scenes.summary: As the ladies separate to dress, Mr. Collins anxiously coaches Elizabeth on simple apparel and hurries everyone, heightening Maria's terror of meeting Lady Catherine.

scenes.title: Walk Across the Park
scenes.summary: The party walks pleasantly across the park to Rosings; Elizabeth resists Mr. Collins's raptures about windows and cost while Maria's and Sir William's alarm grows at the doors.

scenes.title: Reception and Inspection
scenes.summary: Led through hall and antechamber, the visitors are received with condescending authority; Sir William and Maria are awed into silence while Elizabeth calmly observes the imperious mother and sickly, insignificant daughter.

scenes.title: The Splendid Dinner
scenes.summary: After admiring the view from the windows, the party endures a splendid, stiff dinner of sycophantic praise from Collins and Sir William, silent embarrassment from the young women, and gracious satisfaction from Lady Catherine.

scenes.title: Lady Catherine's Interrogation
scenes.summary: In the drawing-room Lady Catherine talks without intermission, dictating on household management, interrogating Elizabeth on sisters, education, governesses, and accomplishments; Elizabeth answers composedly and finally trifles with her, to astonishment.

scenes.title: Cards and Carriage Home
scenes.summary: Tea and dull card parties follow, with Lady Catherine dominating quadrille and Mrs. Jenkinson fussing over Miss de Bourgh; the carriage finally releases them into bows, thanks, and Elizabeth's guarded verdict on Rosings.

scenes.title: Settled Routine at Hunsford
scenes.summary: After Sir William leaves, the Parsonage settles into routine; Collins works in his front room while the ladies sit behind, and Elizabeth realizes Charlotte chose the back sitting-room to keep her husband away, while Collins reports carriages and Miss de Bourgh passing in the lane.

scenes.title: Lady Catherine's Domineering Watch
scenes.summary: The Collinses constantly attend Rosings and endure Lady Catherine's intrusive calls, as she inspects work, furniture, servants, and food; Elizabeth sees her as an unofficial magistrate who scolds cottagers into order.

scenes.title: Quiet Walks and Expected Arrival
scenes.summary: Rosings dinners repeat twice weekly while Elizabeth finds comfort in talks with Charlotte and solitary walks out of Lady Catherine's reach; the quiet fortnight ends with anticipation of Easter and Mr. Darcy's expected arrival.

scenes.title: News from Rosings
scenes.summary: Mr. Collins watches for Darcy's arrival and hurries to Rosings to pay his respects, then returns to the Parsonage unexpectedly accompanied by Darcy and Colonel Fitzwilliam.

scenes.title: A Civil Visit Tested
scenes.summary: The gentlemen visit the Parsonage; while Colonel Fitzwilliam converses pleasantly and Darcy remains reserved, Elizabeth questions Darcy about Jane in London and observes his confusion before they depart.

scenes.title: Easter Evening at Rosings
scenes.summary: After a week of little contact, Elizabeth and the Collinses join the Rosings evening party on Easter-day. Lady Catherine is civil but preoccupied with her nephews, while Colonel Fitzwilliam warmly seeks out Elizabeth and entertains her with lively talk that draws Darcy and Lady Catherine's attention.

scenes.title: Lady Catherine Commands the Music Talk
scenes.summary: Lady Catherine demands to join the music conversation and dominates it with self-praise, claims about Anne's lost talent, and lectures on practice. Darcy praises his sister Georgiana and is left embarrassed and silent by his aunt's ill-breeding toward Elizabeth.

scenes.title: Sparring at the Pianoforte
scenes.summary: At Fitzwilliam's request Elizabeth plays the pianoforte while Darcy watches her intently. Their exchange turns into arch, flirtatious sparring about frightening, exposing character, and Darcy's infamous dancing only four dances at the Hertfordshire ball.

scenes.title: Critique and Polite Endurance
scenes.summary: Lady Catherine interrupts again to criticize Elizabeth's playing and instruct her, praising Anne above her. Elizabeth notes Darcy's lack of romantic interest in Miss de Bourgh and politely endures the remarks, playing on until the carriage takes them home.

scenes.title: An Awkward Call Alone
scenes.summary: Alone at the parsonage, Elizabeth is startled when Mr. Darcy calls by himself, expecting Lady Catherine. Their tête-à-tête is stiff and awkward, moving from Bingley and Netherfield to the Collins marriage and distance from family, growing briefly personal before Darcy withdraws into cold politeness.

scenes.title: Puzzling Over His Visits
scenes.summary: Charlotte and Maria's return ends the strained visit. Charlotte wonders if Darcy is in love with Elizabeth, but his silence makes it doubtful. Both cousins begin calling almost daily, Fitzwilliam clearly enjoying their company while Darcy's silent, staring visits baffle Mrs. Collins, who watches for love and idly considers Fitzwilliam as a match.

scenes.title: Walks in the Park
scenes.summary: Elizabeth is repeatedly surprised by Mr. Darcy during her solitary walks in the park, puzzled by his odd questions about Hunsford and Rosings. She then meets Colonel Fitzwilliam, who joins her to walk back toward the Parsonage.

scenes.title: The Price of a Younger Son
scenes.summary: In light, witty conversation, Elizabeth and Colonel Fitzwilliam debate the power of wealth, self-denial, and the necessity for younger sons to marry women of fortune.

scenes.title: An Imprudent Marriage Prevented
scenes.summary: Talk turns to Darcy and his joint guardianship of Miss Darcy. Fitzwilliam carelessly reveals that Darcy lately congratulated himself on saving a friend from a most imprudent marriage, which Elizabeth suspects means Bingley.

scenes.title: Growing Indignation
scenes.summary: Elizabeth presses for reasons and methods of Darcy's interference, concealing her indignation. She condemns his right to judge his friend's inclination while trying to appear impartial.

scenes.title: Alone with the Truth
scenes.summary: Alone in her room, Elizabeth realizes Darcy was the cause of Jane's suffering and Bingley's separation, blaming his pride about their connections. Overcome with agitation and headache, she stays home from Rosings.

scenes.title: Brooding Resentment Over Jane's Letters
scenes.summary: Alone, Elizabeth re-reads Jane's letters from Kent, marking their lost cheerfulness and nursing anger at Darcy's boast of separating Jane and Bingley, consoled only by his imminent departure and her soon return to Jane.

scenes.title: An Unexpected Entrance Breaks Her Thoughts
scenes.summary: Dismissing thoughts of Colonel Fitzwilliam's departure, Elizabeth is startled by the door bell, expecting him, but is utterly amazed when an agitated Mr. Darcy walks in and begins to speak.

scenes.title: An Arrogant Proposal
scenes.summary: Darcy abruptly declares he has struggled in vain and ardently loves her. Elizabeth is stunned into silence, which he takes as encouragement. He professes long-felt attachment but dwells with pride on her inferiority and family obstacles, turning pity into anger.

scenes.title: Cold Refusal Without Civility
scenes.summary: Elizabeth coldly refuses Darcy, saying she never desired his good opinion. Stung, pale with anger, Darcy struggles for composure and demands why he is rejected with so little civility.

scenes.title: Charge Over Jane and Unrepentant Admission
scenes.summary: Elizabeth charges Darcy with ruining Jane's happiness by dividing her from Bingley. He listens unmoved and admits without remorse that he separated them and rejoices in his success.

scenes.title: The Wickham Accusation and Clash of Pride
scenes.summary: Elizabeth adds her older dislike founded on Wickham's account of Darcy's cruelty in withholding his fortune and independence. Darcy answers with contempt for Wickham's misfortunes, then paces the room defending his honest confession about her inferior connections as natural and just.

scenes.title: Final Rejection and Immovable Dislike
scenes.summary: Elizabeth angrily declares no manner of offer could have tempted her to accept him, tracing her immovable dislike to his arrogance, conceit, and selfish disdain from their first acquaintance.

scenes.title: Abrupt Departure and Tearful Turmoil
scenes.summary: Darcy, mortified and ashamed, apologizes for taking her time and rushes from the house. Left alone, Elizabeth weeps in tumultuous astonishment, gratification, and anger, then flees to her room to avoid observation.

scenes.title: Morning After Turmoil
scenes.summary: Still reeling from Darcy's proposal, Elizabeth seeks solitude in air and exercise, deliberately avoiding the park where Darcy might walk.

scenes.title: The Letter Delivered
scenes.summary: Darcy unexpectedly intercepts Elizabeth at the park gate, silently hands her a letter asking her to read it, and vanishes back into the plantation.

scenes.title: Reading Darcy's Defence
scenes.summary: Alone in the lane, Elizabeth opens Darcy's long letter and begins his defense: denial of renewing his offers, and his accounts of separating Bingley from Jane and of Wickham's true history with Georgiana.

scenes.title: First Reading — Outrage and Denial
scenes.summary: Elizabeth reads Darcy's letter in a fury of prejudice. She dismisses his account of Netherfield as proud and insolent, then reacts to his account of Wickham with astonishment, apprehension and horror, insisting it must be false and hastily putting the letter away unread.

scenes.title: Re-reading — The Will, the Money, and Fitzwilliam's Proof
scenes.summary: Elizabeth compels herself to re-examine Darcy's account of Wickham line by line: the will versus the 3000 pounds in lieu of the living, Wickham's alleged extravagance and profligacy for which she has no counter-proof, and the design on Miss Darcy confirmed by Colonel Fitzwilliam's prior account and offered corroboration.

scenes.title: Recollection — Vanity, Evasion, and Mercenary Views
scenes.summary: Recalling Wickham's own words and conduct, Elizabeth sees his impropriety in confiding to a stranger, his boast of facing Darcy belied by avoiding the Netherfield ball, his spreading the story after the Netherfields left, and his mercenary pursuit of Miss King, while Bingley's testimony and Darcy's consistent character further vindicate Darcy.

scenes.title: Self-Reckoning — Humiliation and Second Sight
scenes.summary: Overwhelmed by shame, Elizabeth condemns her own blindness, vanity and prejudice. On second perusal she accepts Darcy's account of Jane's reserved manner and Bingley, and feels severe mortification at his just reproach of her family's impropriety at Netherfield.

scenes.title: Return Home — Changed and Apart
scenes.summary: After two hours of wandering and painful reconsideration, exhausted Elizabeth returns home resolved to hide her reflections. She learns Darcy has called briefly to take leave and Fitzwilliam waited an hour for her, but she can think only of the letter.

scenes.title: The Diminished Party at Rosings
scenes.summary: The morning after Darcy and the Colonel leave Rosings, Collins reports them in tolerable health. At dinner, Elizabeth privately amuses herself that she might have been Lady Catherine's niece, while Lady Catherine laments the loss of the young men and claims Darcy's attachment to Rosings increases.

scenes.title: Lady Catherine Presses Elizabeth to Stay
scenes.summary: After dinner Lady Catherine notices Elizabeth's low spirits, assumes she dislikes going home, and presses her to extend her stay and ride to London with her; Elizabeth politely refuses, and Lady Catherine lectures on the impropriety of young women travelling post alone.

scenes.title: Lady Catherine Questions the Journey
scenes.summary: Lady Catherine interrogates Elizabeth about servants and changes of horses on their journey; Elizabeth welcomes the required attention as a distraction from her occupied mind and reserves reflection for solitary walks.

scenes.title: Solitary Reckoning
scenes.summary: Alone on solitary walks, Elizabeth studies Darcy's letter until she knows it by heart, torn between indignation at his manner, shame at her own injustice, and compassion for him. Her regret deepens over her family's incorrigible folly, Jane's loss of Bingley, and Wickham's exposed character, leaving her spirits unusually depressed.

scenes.title: Farewell Directions
scenes.summary: During the final week the Hunsford party dines as frequently as ever at Rosings. On the last evening Lady Catherine minutely directs their packing and journey, then parts with great condescension, wishing a good journey and inviting them back next year.

scenes.title: Mr. Collins's Farewell Pomp
scenes.summary: Before the others appear for breakfast, Mr. Collins pays Elizabeth his indispensably necessary parting civilities, apologizing for Hunsford's dullness while boasting of Rosings and his felicity with Charlotte. Elizabeth answers with polite thanks and is relieved when Charlotte's entrance interrupts his self-congratulation.

scenes.title: Leaving Hunsford
scenes.summary: The chaise is made ready and after an affectionate parting Elizabeth and Maria are handed in by Mr. Collins, who stops the door to add humble respects for Rosings. As they drive off, Maria chatters about how much has happened and their many dinners at Rosings, while Elizabeth privately reflects on how much she must conceal.

scenes.title: London Arrival With a Secret
scenes.summary: The journey to Mr. Gardiner's house in London passes quietly and without alarm. Jane looks well but there is no leisure to study her spirits. Elizabeth is tormented by temptation to astonish Jane with Mr. Darcy's proposal, holding back from indecision and fear of grieving her further about Bingley.

scenes.title: Reunion at the Inn
scenes.summary: The sisters reunite at the inn where Kitty and Lydia proudly show off a cold luncheon and Lydia's new bonnet, chattering frivolously about shopping and lamenting the militia's coming removal to Brighton.

scenes.title: Lydia's News About Wickham
scenes.summary: Over luncheon Lydia delivers her capital news that Wickham is safe from marrying Mary King, prompting Jane's mild concern and Elizabeth's shocked self-recognition at her own former prejudice.

scenes.title: The Noisy Ride Home
scenes.summary: Crammed into the carriage for the ride to Longbourn, Lydia dominates with loud, unceasing stories of dances and dressing-up fun, while Elizabeth endures the constant mention of Wickham.

scenes.title: A Kind and Noisy Homecoming Dinner
scenes.summary: The Bennets receive Jane and Elizabeth kindly at home, and a crowded dinner with the Lucases dissolves into chaotic cross-talk over fashions, poultry, and Lydia's loud account of the coach ride from London.

scenes.title: Quiet Dread Over Wickham and Brighton
scenes.summary: Mary gravely dismisses Lydia's pleasures, Elizabeth blocks a walk to Meryton to avoid Wickham while counting on the regiment's removal, and she watches her mother press the Brighton scheme against her father's vague refusal.

scenes.title: Elizabeth's Confession to Jane
scenes.summary: Elizabeth tells Jane of Darcy's proposal and her refusal, then recounts his letter exposing Wickham's wickedness. Jane is grieved for Darcy and shocked by Wickham, struggling to believe ill of either, while Elizabeth admits her prejudice, blindness, and harsh words about Wickham.

scenes.title: The Decision for Silence
scenes.summary: Elizabeth asks Jane whether Wickham's true character should be made public. They agree to stay silent, since Darcy did not authorize disclosure, no one would believe them, and exposure might ruin Wickham forever. Elizabeth keeps Darcy's account of Bingley to herself.

scenes.title: Jane's Quiet Heartbreak
scenes.summary: Elizabeth reflects on Jane's unhappy lingering love for Bingley, while Mrs. Bennet lamentingly declares Bingley undeserving and predicts Jane will die of a broken heart.

scenes.title: Mrs. Bennet on the Collinses
scenes.summary: Mrs. Bennet turns to gossip about the Collinses' comfortable housekeeping and their expectation of inheriting Longbourn, to Elizabeth's curt restraint.

scenes.title: Mourning the Regiment
scenes.summary: With the regiment about to leave Meryton, Kitty and Lydia wail in comic despair and Mrs. Bennet joins their grief and longs for Brighton, while Elizabeth watches with shame and remembers the justice of Darcy's objections.

scenes.title: Invitation to Brighton
scenes.summary: Mrs. Forster invites Lydia to accompany her to Brighton, sending Lydia and Mrs. Bennet into rapture and leaving Kitty repining with envy while Elizabeth and Jane try in vain to reason with her.

scenes.title: A Father's Indifference
scenes.summary: Alarmed by Lydia's levity, Elizabeth privately urges her father to forbid the Brighton trip and warns of disgrace to the whole family, but Mr. Bennet treats it lightly and lets Lydia go to secure peace at home.

scenes.title: Dreams of Brighton
scenes.summary: Unaware of Elizabeth's intervention, Lydia indulges in dazzling fantasies of officers, camp, and flirtation at Brighton, which alone consoles Mrs. Bennet for her husband's refusal to go himself.

scenes.title: Elizabeth's Disillusionment with Wickham
scenes.summary: Seeing Wickham for the last time, Elizabeth feels all former partiality gone, detecting affectation in his gentleness and resenting his renewed idle gallantry as an insult to her vanity and understanding.

scenes.title: Probing Wickham on Darcy and Fitzwilliam
scenes.summary: At the officers' last dinner at Longbourn, Elizabeth coolly mentions Fitzwilliam and Darcy at Rosings to probe Wickham; he betrays surprise and alarm before recovering to disparage Darcy's essentials and ascribe his civility to fear of Lady Catherine and designs on Miss de Bourgh.

scenes.title: Civil Parting and Lydia's Noisy Farewell
scenes.summary: Elizabeth refuses to indulge Wickham's grievances and they part with mutual civility; the party then breaks up as Lydia leaves noisily with Mrs. Forster amid Mrs. Bennet's injunctions and Kitty's envious tears.

scenes.title: Reflections on an Unhappy Marriage
scenes.summary: Elizabeth reflects painfully on her parents' unsuitable marriage, her father's lost affection and mocking detachment, and the disadvantages this brings upon his daughters.

scenes.title: Gloom After the Regiment Departs
scenes.summary: With Wickham and the regiment gone, Elizabeth finds little satisfaction as Mrs. Bennet and Kitty's constant repinings gloom Longbourn, Lydia's promised minute letters prove short and unsatisfying, and Elizabeth fixes her hopes on the Lakes tour as consolation.

scenes.title: Slow Recovery at Longbourn
scenes.summary: After a few weeks, health and cheerfulness return to Longbourn with summer company and engagements, Mrs. Bennet regains her usual serenity, and Kitty recovers enough to enter Meryton without tears.

scenes.title: The Tour Shortened and Begun
scenes.summary: Mrs. Gardiner's letter curtails the Northern tour to Derbyshire, disappointing Elizabeth's hopes for the Lakes until thoughts of Pemberley intrude; the Gardiners at last arrive at Longbourn and set off with Elizabeth in cheerful companionship.

scenes.title: A Proposed Detour to Pemberley
scenes.summary: Near Lambton, Mrs. Gardiner wishes to see Pemberley again and Mr. Gardiner agrees, leaving Elizabeth to be asked for her approbation.

scenes.title: Curiosity Overcomes Dread
scenes.summary: Elizabeth feigns indifference to hide her dread of meeting Mr. Darcy, then privately learns the family is absent and agrees to go out of curiosity.

scenes.title: First Sight of Pemberley
scenes.summary: Driving in with nervous anticipation, Elizabeth sees Pemberley House across the valley for the first time and is overwhelmed by its natural beauty, feeling for a moment what it might mean to be its mistress.

scenes.title: Admitted to Pemberley
scenes.summary: Admitted by the civil housekeeper, Elizabeth tours the lofty, handsome rooms, admiring their tasteful furniture and the beautiful prospect from every window.

scenes.title: Lost Mistress and Lucky Absence
scenes.summary: Elizabeth checks her regret at having lost Pemberley as mistress, then is relieved to hear from Mrs. Reynolds that Darcy is absent until tomorrow.

scenes.title: Miniatures Over the Mantel
scenes.summary: Called to the miniatures, Elizabeth confronts Wickham's likeness and then Darcy's likeness, enduring teasing about knowing Darcy while the housekeeper praises Miss Darcy's beauty and accomplishment.

scenes.title: Never a Cross Word
scenes.summary: Encouraged by Mr. Gardiner, Mrs. Reynolds talks with pride of Darcy and his sister, declaring she never had a cross word from him since he was four and that he was the sweetest-tempered, most generous-hearted boy, leaving Elizabeth astonished at praise so opposite to her opinion of him.

scenes.title: Best Landlord and Master
scenes.summary: As they go up the great staircase, Mrs. Reynolds dwells on Darcy as the best landlord and best master, never proud, to Elizabeth's wonder, while Mrs. Gardiner whispers that this fine account is inconsistent with Wickham's story of his behaviour.

scenes.title: The Gallery Portrait
scenes.summary: Shown the pretty sitting-room prepared for Miss Darcy and then the gallery, Elizabeth lingers before Darcy's smiling portrait, softening toward him with gratitude as she considers how much happiness depends on him.

scenes.title: Unexpected Meeting
scenes.summary: Walking back to the river, the party is shocked by Darcy's sudden, blushing appearance a day early; after an agonizingly awkward exchange he leaves, and Elizabeth walks on distracted before spotting him approaching again.

scenes.title: Relations Introduced Without Flinching
scenes.summary: Mrs. Gardiner introduces Darcy to her friends, watching for his reaction on learning they are Elizabeth's relations; to her surprise he bears it with fortitude, turns back with them, and enters into conversation with Mr. Gardiner, to Elizabeth's triumph and pleasure.

scenes.title: Fishing Civilly Offered
scenes.summary: Talk turns to fishing, and Darcy with great civility invites Mr. Gardiner to fish at Pemberley as often as he pleases, offering tackle and advice; Elizabeth is gratified and astonished, wondering at the cause of his altered manners.

scenes.title: Sister at Lambton Proposed
scenes.summary: Walking by the river, Darcy joins Elizabeth, explains his unexpected arrival, names Bingley among tomorrow's party, and asks leave to introduce his sister at Lambton; after civil talk they reach the carriage, decline refreshment, and part with utmost politeness as Darcy hands them in.

scenes.title: Praise on the Drive Home
scenes.summary: On the drive home Mr. and Mrs. Gardiner declare Darcy infinitely superior to expectation, polite and attentive, and press Elizabeth on why she had called him disagreeable and less handsome than Wickham.

scenes.title: Vindication over Wickham
scenes.summary: Mrs. Gardiner cannot reconcile Darcy's pleasing, dignified look with cruelty to Wickham, prompting Elizabeth to partly vindicate him by relating his pecuniary transactions with Wickham on guarded Kent authority.

scenes.title: Wonder in the Evening Alone
scenes.summary: Mrs. Gardiner turns to old Lambton acquaintance for the evening, leaving Elizabeth alone to wonder at Darcy's civility and above all his wish that she meet his sister.

scenes.title: An Anxious Morning Watch
scenes.summary: Elizabeth waits anxiously at the Lambton inn expecting Darcy to bring his sister later, but the Darcy carriage arrives that very morning. Flustered and fearful of being seen, she tells her astonished uncle and aunt, whose suspicions of Darcy's partiality for her are newly awakened.

scenes.title: Miss Darcy Is Shy, Not Proud
scenes.summary: Darcy presents his sister, and Elizabeth is astonished to find Georgiana exceedingly shy rather than proud, able to utter scarcely more than monosyllables, though graceful, womanly, and gentle.

scenes.title: Bingley's Cordial Return
scenes.summary: Bingley arrives with unaffected cordiality that dispels Elizabeth's old anger, while the Gardiners observe Darcy and Elizabeth closely and become convinced that Darcy is overflowing with love.

scenes.title: A Tender Recollection of Jane
scenes.summary: Elizabeth watches Bingley for traces of Jane, sees no particular regard between him and Georgiana, and interprets his regretful remark about the eight months since the Netherfield dance as tender recollection of Jane.

scenes.title: Darcy's Humble Attentiveness
scenes.summary: Bingley quietly asks after her sisters with meaningful looks, while Elizabeth marvels at Darcy's humble complaisance in courting the Gardiners' good opinion, so changed from Hunsford, Netherfield, and Rosings.

scenes.title: The Invitation to Dine at Pemberley
scenes.summary: After above half an hour, Darcy has Georgiana join him in inviting the Gardiners and Elizabeth to dine at Pemberley, which Mrs. Gardiner accepts, and Elizabeth, hearing Bingley's delight at seeing her again, reflects on the visit with satisfaction.

scenes.title: Reconsidering Darcy After Dark
scenes.summary: After the visitors leave, the Gardiners privately revise their opinion of Darcy, moved by his politeness and favorable local reports contrasting with Wickham's debts. Alone into the night, Elizabeth lies awake transforming respect into gratitude and affection for Darcy, while plans are made to return Miss Darcy's call at Pemberley the next morning.

scenes.title: An Awkward Call at Pemberley
scenes.summary: Elizabeth dreads Miss Bingley's jealous civility as the party enters Pemberley's saloon. Georgiana receives them with shy embarrassment, conversation stalls until Mrs. Annesley and refreshments ease it, while Elizabeth anxiously awaits and then regrets Mr. Darcy's entrance.

scenes.title: Miss Bingley's Barbed Remark
scenes.summary: Darcy joins the party amid watchful curiosity and tries to bring Elizabeth and Georgiana together. Miss Bingley launches a sneering remark about the militia to invoke Wickham and discompose Elizabeth, causing distress to Elizabeth, Darcy, and Georgiana, before Elizabeth's composure restores calm.

scenes.title: Darcy's Defense and the Silent Drive Home
scenes.summary: After the visit ends, Miss Bingley criticizes Elizabeth's looks to Darcy and his sister, but Darcy openly defends Elizabeth as one of the handsomest women he knows and leaves Bingley humiliated. On the drive home, Elizabeth and Mrs. Gardiner discuss everyone except Darcy himself, though both long to speak of him.

scenes.title: The Two Letters from Longbourn
scenes.summary: After days of disappointment, Elizabeth receives two letters from Jane at Lambton. The first reports Lydia's elopement from Brighton with Wickham, supposedly for Scotland; the second, written a day later, brings far worse intelligence that they were traced only toward London and likely never meant to marry.

scenes.title: Too Ill to Follow
scenes.summary: Still reeling from Jane's letter, Elizabeth rushes to find Mr. Gardiner and collides with Darcy at the door. Trembling and unwell, she sends the servant for her uncle and aunt while Darcy, alarmed by her pallor, refuses to leave her.

scenes.title: Confessing Lydia's Elopement
scenes.summary: In tears, Elizabeth confesses that Lydia has eloped from Brighton with Wickham and is likely ruined. She bitterly blames herself for concealing Wickham's true character, while Darcy listens in shocked, grieved silence.

scenes.title: A Cold Farewell
scenes.summary: Darcy falls into gloomy, silent meditation and withdraws with restrained compassion. Elizabeth reads his condemnation and understands the disgrace must end his regard for her, even as she realizes she could have loved him. He takes his leave from Pemberley.

scenes.title: Reflection on Lydia as Easy Prey
scenes.summary: Alone after Darcy's departure, Elizabeth reflects with regret and anguish on Lydia's elopement, concluding Wickham never meant to marry her and that Lydia's want of virtue and understanding made her an easy prey.

scenes.title: Resolve to Hasten Home
scenes.summary: Wild to be at home, Elizabeth receives the alarmed Gardiners, shares Jane's letters, gains her uncle's promise of help, abandons the Pemberley engagement, and hurries through preparations to quit Lambton for Longbourn.

scenes.title: Hoping Wickham Means Marriage
scenes.summary: Driving from town, Mr. Gardiner argues Wickham would not risk honour, regiment, and friends for a dishonourable elopement, and Mrs. Gardiner comes round to hoping for a private London marriage. Elizabeth answers that Wickham cares only for interest and will not marry a penniless girl, that Lydia has no brothers to fear and a negligent father, and that Lydia's youth, vanity, and ill education leave her vulnerable to Wickham's charm, profligacy, and lies about Darcy and Pemberley.

scenes.title: No Fondness Before Brighton
scenes.summary: Asked if Lydia and Wickham showed fondness before Brighton, Elizabeth says there was no symptom of particular affection on either side, only Lydia's early general admiration which gave way when Wickham paid her no distinction and other officers favoured her.

scenes.title: Hasty Journey Home
scenes.summary: Consumed by self-reproach, Elizabeth travels with her aunt and uncle to Longbourn, where the little Gardiners' joyful capers give a brief pleasing welcome.

scenes.title: Reunion with Jane
scenes.summary: Elizabeth rushes in to embrace Jane in tears and asks at once for news of the fugitives, learning her father is in London, her mother is shaken upstairs, and no intelligence has yet come.

scenes.title: Tears and Invectives in Mrs. Bennet's Chamber
scenes.summary: In the drawing-room Jane has no intelligence to give but clings to sanguine hope, then in Mrs. Bennet's apartment the family meets tears, lamentations, invectives against Wickham, blame of all but herself, and terror that Mr. Bennet will fight Wickham and be killed.

scenes.title: Mr. Gardiner's Promise and Counsel of Moderation
scenes.summary: Mr. Gardiner promises to go to London the next day to assist Mr. Bennet in recovering Lydia, counsels against useless alarm, listens to Mrs. Bennet's pleas to make them marry and keep Mr. Bennet from fighting, and recommends moderation in hope and fear.

scenes.title: Cold Comfort at Dinner
scenes.summary: At dinner Mary and Kitty appear calm, Kitty fretful and Mary offering sententious consolation about female virtue and ruin, which Elizabeth receives in amazed, oppressed silence.

scenes.title: Sisters Compare Accounts
scenes.summary: Alone together, Elizabeth and Jane compare accounts of Colonel Forster, Denny, and Lydia's foreknowledge, and Elizabeth laments that their secrecy about Wickham's true character allowed this to happen.

scenes.title: Lydia's Letter and the Search
scenes.summary: Jane produces Lydia's thoughtless, laughing Gretna Green note, confirming her serious but reckless intent, then describes the household's shock and her father's hurried plans to trace the hackney coach from Epsom and Clapham.

scenes.title: Anxious Waiting at Longbourn
scenes.summary: At Longbourn the family waits in vain for news from Mr. Bennet, while the Gardiners support them and Meryton turns viciously against Wickham, deepening Elizabeth and Jane's despair over Lydia.

scenes.title: Fruitless Search in London
scenes.summary: Mr. Gardiner writes from London that Mr. Bennet's searches in Epsom, Clapham and hotels have failed, asking for clues to Wickham's relations, which Elizabeth cannot provide as each post brings fresh anxiety.

scenes.title: Mr. Collins's Cruel Condolence
scenes.summary: Jane opens a condoling letter from Mr. Collins, which coldly blames Lydia's indulgence and bad disposition, rejoices he escaped the disgrace, and urges casting her off forever.

scenes.title: Wickham's Gaming Debts Revealed
scenes.summary: Mr. Gardiner reports Colonel Forster's news that Wickham has no traceable relations and has left considerable gaming debts at Brighton, horrifying Jane.

scenes.title: A Spiritless Return and Private Grief
scenes.summary: Mr. Bennet agrees to return home to Mrs. Bennet's dismay, while Elizabeth privately grieves that Darcy's loss compounds the shame of Lydia's ruin.

scenes.title: A Father's Remorse
scenes.summary: Mr. Bennet returns with philosophic composure, breaking silence at tea to take full blame for Lydia's flight and acknowledge Elizabeth's foresight, until interrupted fetching tea.

scenes.title: Bitter Jest at Kitty's Expense
scenes.summary: Mr. Bennet's guilt turns to bitter, sardonic jesting about misfortune, threatening Kitty with no officers, no balls and enforced rationality, leaving her in tears before a mock promise.

scenes.title: News of an Express
scenes.summary: In the shrubbery, Mrs. Hill astonishes Jane and Elizabeth with news that an express has arrived for Mr. Bennet from Mr. Gardiner in town, sparking urgent hope.

scenes.title: The Chase for Father
scenes.summary: The sisters race through the house and lawn after their father toward the copse, breathless for news, and Elizabeth begs him to share his letter.

scenes.title: Gardiner's Letter Read Aloud
scenes.summary: Mr. Bennet has Elizabeth read Mr. Gardiner's letter aloud: Lydia and Wickham are found, unmarried but to be married if Mr. Bennet agrees to settlement terms.

scenes.title: Counting the True Cost
scenes.summary: Walking home, father and daughters react with relief and suspicion, realizing Wickham must have been bribed and that generous Uncle Gardiner must have paid heavily.

scenes.title: Sisters Reckon in Private
scenes.summary: Alone in the breakfast-room, Jane comforts herself that Wickham must feel regard, while Elizabeth mourns Lydia's disgrace and honors the Gardiners' sacrifice.

scenes.title: Carrying Good News Upstairs
scenes.summary: The girls get their father's leave to tell their mother, and upstairs read the letter to Mrs. Bennet, Mary, and Kitty, igniting Mrs. Bennet's ecstatic joy.

scenes.title: Maternal Ecstasy and Quiet Relief
scenes.summary: Mrs. Bennet erupts into wedding-clothes plans, gossip visits, and punch for servants, while Elizabeth withdraws to reflect thankfully that Lydia's fate is no worse.

scenes.title: The Regret for Nothing Saved
scenes.summary: Mr. Bennet regrets never saving for his wife and children, blames his failure for making Lydia dependent on her uncle, resolves to learn what his brother-in-law has spent and repay him, and recalls how hope for a son and lack of economy left the family unprovided.

scenes.title: A Grateful Assent at Small Cost
scenes.summary: Mr. Bennet gratefully approves the marriage settlement for Lydia, surprised that Wickham can be secured with so little yearly loss to himself, and quickly dispatches his assent while asking what he owes his brother but refusing any message to Lydia.

scenes.title: Spiteful Wishes and Fine Muslins
scenes.summary: News of Lydia's imminent marriage spreads through house and neighbourhood with spiteful amusement, while Mrs. Bennet, downstairs again in oppressively high spirits, triumphs without shame and talks only of muslins, carriages, servants, and a grand house for her daughter.

scenes.title: No Admittance at Longbourn
scenes.summary: As Mrs. Bennet rejects houses as too small or too far, Mr. Bennet waits then sternly forbids Wickham and Lydia ever being received at Longbourn, and after long dispute refuses any money for wedding clothes, to Mrs. Bennet's horror.

scenes.title: Love Lost to Disgrace
scenes.summary: Elizabeth mourns in private that Lydia's disgrace has made any union with Darcy impossible, realizing too late that he suited her perfectly and that his esteem is now lost.

scenes.title: Wickham's Removal to the North
scenes.summary: Mr. Gardiner writes that Wickham will quit the militia for an ensigncy in a regular regiment in the North, where friends will assist him, and that he has pledged himself to pay Wickham's Brighton and Meryton debts within a week.

scenes.title: Mrs. Bennet's Disappointment
scenes.summary: Mr. Bennet and his daughters approve Wickham's distance from the militia, but Mrs. Bennet is disappointed to lose Lydia's company in Hertfordshire and among her friends and favourite officers.

scenes.title: Persuaded to Receive the Newlyweds
scenes.summary: Jane and Elizabeth persuade the reluctant Mr. Bennet to receive Lydia and Wickham at Longbourn after their marriage, delighting Mrs. Bennet, though Elizabeth dreads meeting Wickham.

scenes.title: Dreaded Arrival
scenes.summary: Jane and Elizabeth dread their married sister's return, imagining the shame she ought to feel; the family gathers anxiously in the breakfast room as the carriage arrives.

scenes.title: The Shameless Newlyweds
scenes.summary: Lydia bursts in unabashed and exultant, demanding congratulations and flaunting her marriage, while Wickham charms with easy assurance; her father is stern, her sisters mortified, and Elizabeth flees the room in disgust before Lydia claims Jane's precedence as a married woman.
