scenes.title: Unequal Affection
scenes.summary: The visit is set for only ten days before Wickham rejoins his regiment; Mrs. Bennet bustles with parties while Elizabeth reflects that Lydia loves Wickham far more than he loves her, and that distress must have driven him to elope.

scenes.title: Lydia Tells Her Wedding
scenes.summary: Lydia offers Elizabeth an account of her wedding at St. Clement's, describing her fuss, her aunt preaching while she dressed, and thinking only of Wickham and his blue coat.

scenes.title: A Secret Betrayed
scenes.summary: Elizabeth is amazed to hear Darcy was to come with Wickham; Lydia realizes she broke a promised secret, Jane and Elizabeth feign disinterest, and Elizabeth runs away rather than question her further.

scenes.title: Burning Curiosity
scenes.summary: Alone with wild conjectures about why Darcy attended Lydia's wedding, Elizabeth cannot bear suspense and writes urgently to her aunt for an explanation, vowing to resort to tricks if refused, while Jane's delicacy keeps her from discussing it.

scenes.title: The Letter Reveals Darcy's Secret
scenes.summary: Alone in the copse, Elizabeth reads Mrs. Gardiner's long letter revealing that Darcy hunted Lydia and Wickham in London, bribed Mrs. Younge for their direction, and paid Wickham's debts and commission. Overwhelmed by fluttering pleasure, shame, and pride, she grasps that Darcy did it all and must now abhor connection with Wickham.

scenes.title: Interrupted by Wickham
scenes.summary: Wickham overtakes Elizabeth on her walk and forces awkward brotherly civility. They trade polite barbs about Pemberley, Mrs. Reynolds, and Darcy's unexplained presence in town last month, with Elizabeth deflecting and hoping to silence him.

scenes.title: A Pointed Truce About the Past
scenes.summary: The talk sharpens as Elizabeth counters Wickham's fishing about Lambton and Kympton living, confronting him with the truth that the living was conditional and that he had refused orders. Hurrying to the house, she closes the past with a smiling truce and a gallant kiss of her hand.

scenes.title: Farewell to the Wickhams
scenes.summary: Wickham and Lydia depart for Newcastle. Mrs. Bennet laments the separation while Mr. Bennet mocks Wickham with ironic praise and Elizabeth teases her mother about married daughters.

scenes.title: Tidings of Bingley's Return
scenes.summary: News circulates that Mr. Bingley will return to Netherfield to shoot for weeks. Mrs. Bennet is thrown into hopeful agitation and pumps her sister Mrs. Philips for confirmation.

scenes.title: Jane's Uneasy Indifference
scenes.summary: Alone together, Jane insists Bingley's coming affects her with neither pleasure nor pain and dreads others' remarks. Elizabeth doubts her and sees her sister's spirits are disturbed and unequal.

scenes.title: To Visit or Not to Visit
scenes.summary: Mrs. Bennet presses Mr. Bennet to wait on Bingley, but he refuses last year's fool's errand. She resolves to invite him to dinner instead, while Jane confesses to Elizabeth how much her mother's constant talk makes her suffer.

scenes.title: Bingley Sighted from the Window
scenes.summary: Mrs. Bennet eagerly watches for Bingley after his return to Hertfordshire and spots him riding toward Longbourn from her window. She calls her daughters, and Elizabeth discovers to her shock that Mr. Darcy is riding with him.

scenes.title: An Unwelcome Friend Acknowledged
scenes.summary: Kitty identifies Darcy's arrival as Mrs. Bennet loudly proclaims her dislike while promising civility for Bingley's sake. Jane and Elizabeth endure awkward distress in silence, Elizabeth concealing her secret gratitude and changed feelings toward Darcy.

scenes.title: Cold Civility and Mortifying Talk
scenes.summary: Elizabeth anxiously watches Jane receive Bingley with composed propriety. Darcy looks grave and is almost silent, while Bingley looks pleased yet embarrassed. Mrs. Bennet receives Bingley with excessive civility and Darcy with cold ceremony, then mortifies Elizabeth with vulgar talk of Lydia's marriage notice and an officious invitation to shoot on Mr. Bennet's manor.

scenes.title: Misery Relieved by Rekindled Admiration
scenes.summary: Overwhelmed with shame at her mother, Elizabeth wishes never to see either gentleman again, but gains relief on observing Bingley's attention to Jane steadily rekindle as he finds her as handsome, good-natured, and unaffected as before.

scenes.title: A Dinner Secured
scenes.summary: As the gentlemen leave, Mrs. Bennet secures them for dinner at Longbourn and reproaches Bingley for his broken engagement, while noting Bingley's renewed admiration for Jane and regretting she did not keep them that day.

scenes.title: Vexed Walk and Sisterly Resolve
scenes.summary: Alone after the call, Elizabeth broods vexedly over Darcy's cold silence, then Jane joins her insisting she is now perfectly easy and will meet both men only as indifferent acquaintance.

scenes.title: The Dinner Table Watch
scenes.summary: At the crowded Longbourn dinner, Bingley chooses to sit by Jane to Elizabeth's triumph, while Darcy remains distant and formal near Mrs. Bennet, giving Elizabeth painful anxiety.

scenes.title: Anxious Waiting for the Gentlemen
scenes.summary: Elizabeth waits anxiously in the drawing-room for the gentlemen to join the ladies, hoping for a chance to speak properly with Darcy. When they enter, the crowded tea-table leaves no vacant place near her, a girl whispers to keep the men away, and Darcy walks to another part of the room while she watches him with envy and self-reproach.

scenes.title: Coffee Cups and Lost to the Whist Table
scenes.summary: Convinced Darcy will never renew his addresses after refusal, Elizabeth revives when he returns his coffee cup and asks briefly after Georgiana at Pemberley. Conversation fails into silence and he walks away, and her last hope of private talk ends when Mrs. Bennet claims him for whist, leaving them confined at different tables.

scenes.title: Mrs. Bennet's Triumph
scenes.summary: Left alone after the Netherfield gentlemen depart early, Mrs. Bennet exults over the dinner, Bingley's attentions, and her certainty of Jane's coming engagement.

scenes.title: Jane Protests Indifference
scenes.summary: Jane insists she now enjoys Bingley only as an agreeable acquaintance without design, while Elizabeth teases her disbelief, ending in playful reproach about indifference and confidence.

scenes.title: Bingley Returns Alone
scenes.summary: Mr. Bingley calls alone, in high spirits, and after declining dinner accepts Mrs. Bennet's eager invitation to come tomorrow, reviving hope for Jane.

scenes.title: Frantic Preparations
scenes.summary: Bingley arrives early while the ladies are undressed, prompting frantic comedy as Mrs. Bennet rushes Jane downstairs while Jane insists on waiting for a sister.

scenes.title: A Transparent Contrivance
scenes.summary: After tea Mrs. Bennet winks at Elizabeth and Kitty to force them to leave Jane and Bingley alone, then drags Kitty and Elizabeth from the drawing-room into the hall.

scenes.title: A Charming But Inconclusive Evening
scenes.summary: Left ineffectually alone, Bingley is charming but makes no declaration, then arranges to shoot with Mr. Bennet, leaving Elizabeth hopeful that Darcy has consented to the match.

scenes.title: An Awkward Discovery by the Hearth
scenes.summary: Bingley spends the morning with Mr. Bennet and stays to dinner. In the evening Mrs. Bennet schemes to leave him alone with Jane while the others play cards. Returning from writing her letter, Elizabeth finds Jane and Bingley in earnest private talk by the hearth; confused, Bingley whispers to Jane and hurries out.

scenes.title: Jane's Happy Confession
scenes.summary: Alone with Elizabeth, Jane embraces her and confesses she is engaged and the happiest creature in the world. Elizabeth congratulates her warmly. Jane rushes to tell her mother first, while Bingley goes to her father, leaving Elizabeth to reflect on the happy end to months of suspense.

scenes.title: Family Celebration
scenes.summary: Bingley returns from her father's approval to claim Elizabeth as a sister. The family celebrates at supper, with Mr. Bennet's dry congratulations and Mrs. Bennet's ecstatic effusions over Jane's fortune.

scenes.title: Happy Aftermath and Confidences
scenes.summary: Bingley becomes a daily visitor while Jane confides how his sisters hid her presence in London. Elizabeth rejoices but hides Darcy's interference, as news spreads and the Bennets are pronounced the luckiest family.

scenes.title: An Unwelcome Visitor
scenes.summary: A strange chaise arrives at Longbourn. Bingley and Jane escape to the shrubbery while Lady Catherine enters ungraciously, exchanges stiff civilities with Mrs. Bennet, criticizes the house and park, refuses refreshment, and demands a private walk with Elizabeth.

scenes.title: Walk to the Copse
scenes.summary: Elizabeth leads Lady Catherine in hostile silence along the gravel walk to the copse, bracing herself as her ladyship prepares to speak her purpose.

scenes.title: The Accusation
scenes.summary: Alone in the copse, Lady Catherine accuses Elizabeth of scheming to marry Darcy, cites the circulating report, and insists Elizabeth deny any foundation and promise contradiction.

scenes.title: Defiance of Rank
scenes.summary: The quarrel escalates over Darcy's claimed engagement to Anne de Bourgh from infancy. Lady Catherine invokes honour, decorum, and family disgrace; Elizabeth coolly refuses to be intimidated and defends her right to choose.

scenes.title: The Refused Promise
scenes.summary: Pressed on her inferior connections and asked to declare she is not engaged, Elizabeth admits she is not but steadfastly refuses to promise never to marry Darcy, rejecting Lady Catherine's authority over her.

scenes.title: Insult and Departure
scenes.summary: Lady Catherine plays her last card, insulting Lydia's elopement and the pollution of Pemberley. Elizabeth ends the interview, walks back in resentful silence, and receives a furious parting threat at the carriage.

scenes.title: Aftermath Upstairs
scenes.summary: Elizabeth re-enters the house as the carriage drives away and meets her mother's eager, oblivious questions, forcing her to conceal the true substance of the confrontation.

scenes.title: Fear After Lady Catherine's Threat
scenes.summary: Alone after Lady Catherine's extraordinary visit, Elizabeth replays it incessantly, tracing the Darcy engagement rumor to Lucas Lodge gossip, and sinks into fear that Lady Catherine will appeal to Darcy and that his pride and sense of dignity will make him give her up.

scenes.title: A Father's Mysterious Letter
scenes.summary: The next morning Mr Bennet stops Elizabeth with a letter in hand and leads her to the fireplace, teasing her about being on the brink of matrimony; Elizabeth flushes, fearing and half-hoping it is explanation from Darcy himself.

scenes.title: Mr Collins's Pompous Letter
scenes.summary: Mr Bennet teases Elizabeth with a letter from Mr Collins, reading his congratulations on Jane's nuptials and his pompous hint of another illustrious match for Elizabeth which Lady Catherine de Bourgh does not view with a friendly eye.

scenes.title: Laughter to Hide a Wounded Heart
scenes.summary: Mr Bennet names Mr Darcy as the supposed admirer and laughs at the absurdity given Darcy's indifference and Elizabeth's dislike, while Elizabeth forces laughter to hide her hurt and her fear that she has fancied too much of Darcy's regard.

scenes.title: The Walk Sets Out
scenes.summary: Bingley brings Darcy with him to Longbourn, and to be alone with Jane proposes a walk. Mrs. Bennet and Mary stay behind, the other five set out, with Bingley and Jane soon lagging behind while Elizabeth, Kitty, and Darcy go ahead in silence.

scenes.title: Alone to Thank Him
scenes.summary: Kitty leaves to call on Maria Lucas, leaving Elizabeth alone with Darcy. Elizabeth thanks him for his secret kindness to Lydia, and Darcy replies that he thought only of her.

scenes.title: A Second Proposal Accepted
scenes.summary: Darcy asks if her feelings are unchanged since April, and Elizabeth joyfully accepts his renewed assurances. In delight he explains that Lady Catherine's visit to London to complain of Elizabeth paradoxically taught him to hope, since her refusal to promise to reject him proved she was not irrevocably decided against him.

scenes.title: Sharing Blame for That Evening
scenes.summary: Laughing, Elizabeth admits to abusing Darcy to his relations, Darcy declares his own conduct at Hunsford merited the severest reproof, and Elizabeth proposes they share the blame and note their improved civility.

scenes.title: Tortured by Her Reproof
scenes.summary: Darcy confesses her reproof about behaving in a more gentleman-like manner has tortured him for months, and Elizabeth, ashamed of her harsh refusal, begs him not to repeat what she then said.

scenes.title: The Letter and Humbled Pride
scenes.summary: Talk turns to Darcy's letter: its gradual removal of her prejudice, his wish to burn it, and its bitterness of spirit. Elizabeth urges forgetting unpleasant circumstances, prompting Darcy's deep self-accusation of lifelong selfishness, pride, and conceit, and his gratitude that she humbled and reformed him.

scenes.title: Pemberley Remembered
scenes.summary: Darcy admits his vanity in expecting her acceptance, recalls his surprise and civility at Pemberley to win forgiveness, and tells of Georgiana's delight in her and his resolve formed at the Derbyshire inn to follow her in search of Lydia. Absorbed, they walk miles until their watches warn them home.

scenes.title: News of Jane and Bingley
scenes.summary: Turning to Jane and Bingley, Darcy shares his delight at their engagement and confesses how on the eve of going to London he told Bingley of his former interference, his mistake about Jane's indifference, and his concealment of Jane's winter in town. Elizabeth smiles at his easy direction of his friend as they reach the house and part.

scenes.title: A Quiet Evening of Secret Happiness
scenes.summary: Elizabeth returns deflecting questions about her walk. The evening passes quietly, with Darcy restrained and Elizabeth agitated, happy yet dreading how her family will receive the engagement.

scenes.title: Jane's Incredulity
scenes.summary: At night Elizabeth confides her engagement to Darcy to Jane, who is absolutely incredulous. Elizabeth insists she is in earnest, says her former dislike is to be forgot, and Jane begins to believe her while asking if she can truly be happy with him.

scenes.title: Assurances of Affection
scenes.summary: Elizabeth reassures Jane that she marries with affection and will be the happiest couple, satisfies her with solemn assurances of attachment, and reveals Darcy's share in Lydia's marriage. Jane is finally convinced and overjoyed, and they spend half the night in conversation.

scenes.title: Mrs Bennet's Convenient Proposal
scenes.summary: Next morning Mrs Bennet complains of disagreeable Mr Darcy always coming with Bingley and urges Elizabeth to walk out with him to leave Jane free. Bingley betrays he knows the secret, and a walk to Oakham Mount is arranged for Darcy and Elizabeth.

scenes.title: Seeking Mr Bennet's Consent in the Library
scenes.summary: Elizabeth and Darcy resolve during their walk to ask Mr Bennet that evening. Darcy follows him to the library, leaving Elizabeth in misery until summoned. Facing her father's grave disbelief, she earnestly assures him of her love and esteem for Darcy and wins his consent.

scenes.title: Telling of Darcy and Lydia and Finding Relief
scenes.summary: To complete the favourable impression, Elizabeth tells her father of Darcy's voluntary aid to Lydia. Astonished and relieved of expense, he teases her about Mr Collins's letter and lets her go, and she recovers in her room before rejoining the family with composure.

scenes.title: Mrs Bennet Transformed by Ten Thousand a Year
scenes.summary: Elizabeth tells her mother at night. After stunned silence, Mrs Bennet erupts in rapture over wealth, jewels, carriages, three daughters married and ten thousand a year, insisting on a special licence and asking what dish Darcy likes.

scenes.title: A New Ease at Longbourn
scenes.summary: The next day passes better than feared, with Mrs Bennet awed into deferential silence toward Darcy. Mr Bennet takes pains to know him and rises in esteem, closing with wry praise of his three sons-in-law.

scenes.title: How Could You Begin?
scenes.summary: Elizabeth playfully presses Darcy to explain how he fell in love with her despite her rudeness, and they tease each other about shyness, embarrassment, Lydia's gratitude, Lady Catherine's interference, and his return to Netherfield.

scenes.title: Letters of Happiness
scenes.summary: Elizabeth joyfully writes to Mrs. Gardiner announcing her engagement and inviting the Gardiners to Pemberley, while Darcy writes stiffly to Lady Catherine and Mr. Bennet dryly informs Mr. Collins.

scenes.title: Congratulations and Forbearance
scenes.summary: Insincere congratulations arrive from Miss Bingley and sincere delight from Miss Darcy, the Collinses flee Lady Catherine's anger to Lucas Lodge, and Elizabeth shields Darcy from vulgar attentions while dreaming of Pemberley.

scenes.title: Happy Settlements After the Weddings
scenes.summary: A warm, contented epilogue surveying the fates of all the families after the double marriage: Mrs. Bennet's delighted pride, Mr. Bennet's visits to Pemberley, Jane and Bingley's move near Derbyshire, Kitty's improvement, Mary's quiet life at home, Lydia and Wickham's unsettled extravagance softened by help from Elizabeth, Jane and Darcy, Miss Bingley's renewed civility, Georgiana's loving sisterhood with Elizabeth, Lady Catherine's eventual reconciliation, and lasting intimacy with the Gardiners.
